utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-00-41-PT, the Prosecutor versus Pasko Ljubicic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ljubicic, can you hear me in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. You will have the opportunity to speak during the Status Conference. Thank you very much. Can I please have the appearances, first with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Mark Harmon, representing the Prosecutor. Appearing with me is Ms. Carmela Annink-Javier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my name is Tomislav Jonjic. I am Defence counsel for this accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So your name is Janjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: J-O-N-J-I-C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Now it's my turn to introduce myself. I'm the Pre-Trial Judge in this case. My name is Amin El Mahdi, and as you know, I've been appointed as the Pre-Trial Judge in this case, and I believe that this stage of the proceedings, and you will share my view, I'm sure, is absolutely vital for the conduct of the trial. So I'm not going to read again the decision that you have certainly read, and with this decision, the Chamber ruled on the objection by the Defence about the form of the indictment. The Prosecution has a period of time to submit the amended indictment, and there is also a period of time, then, and during which I hope that the Defence will respond if the case -- if it's necessary. I believe that today's hearing mainly serves the purpose of speeding up the proceedings, and I would suggest that the agenda for today's conference is as follows: First of all, the disclosure of exhibits, of evidence; secondly, the preparation of the Defence; and thirdly, I will give Mr. Ljubicic the opportunity to speak and to tell us what he has to say at this stage of the pre-trial phase. Now, about disclosure, I would like to ask Mr. Harmon to give me some information about what stage we are at in disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, I'd be glad to. We're at a very early stage of disclosure. On the 19th of December, we disclosed the confirming materials to the Defence, and we are undertaking steps to disclose additional statements of witnesses to the Defence. We are somewhat handicapped by virtue of the fact that a motion that we filed on the 11th of February, 2002, entitled the Prosecutor's Motion for Order of Non-disclosure, has not been decided upon, and in that particular motion, we requested five measures to be taken in respect of materials that had been disclosed. So we are waiting for a decision in respect of that particular application by my office. In respect of identifying potential 92 bis statements, matters that are subject to judicial notice, and specifically adjudicated facts, we are in the process of identifying those matters, and we will submit to the Defence, upon completion of those efforts, a set of items that include statements, items for judicial notice, and adjudicated facts, and they can consider those and perhaps we can embark on a proceeding that will be shortened as opposed to a lengthy proceeding. So I can inform Your Honour that is the status thus far of our efforts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Harmon. So if I understand correctly, the Defence is, in principle, not opposed to what you suggest, but - and we'll come to that point later on - but the Defence reserves itself the right for -- on a case-by-case basis or for a specific document to object, keeping in mind the interests of justice. So what I hear is very comforting, because everybody, starting with you, state that the procedure has really started, and I believe that all of us, with your help, all of us will be able to speed up the procedure. Thank you very much, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jonjic, you've heard what Mr. Harmon had to say. I am confident. I don't think that you will put forward a major objection, but you are keeping the possibility to submit an objection as the case may be. If it's in the interests of justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is right, Your Honour. We have no major objections to the process as it has been taking place so far. I just wish to say that the Defence, bearing in mind, of course, the position in which the Prosecution is in and the decision of the Trial Chamber on the preliminary motion and the fact that no decision has yet been made on their motion, the Defence has addressed a request to the OTP for disclosure of the statements of witnesses, parts of which have been included in the confirming material. But we are aware of the difficulties the Prosecution would have and still we hope that we will receive those statements within a relatively short time. That's all for now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you very much. But what do you mean by "difficulty"?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. No, there is no difficulty. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the fair way to deal with this, the fair solution, is to ask Mr. Fourmy to organise meetings between the parties and to make sure that disclosure takes place as quickly as possible, keeping in mind, obviously, the situation of the Prosecution, and enabling the Defence to prepare its case properly. And I fully trust Mr. Fourmy in his capacity to do this, Mr. Fourmy, who is our Senior Legal Officer, and the Chamber is very lucky to benefit from the help of Mr. Fourmy in this case. I would therefore like to invite the parties and to invite Mr. Fourmy to go ahead, and I would like everyone to work in the spirit of cooperation in order to define a framework for the case to develop in a reasonable period of time, reasonable for everyone concerned. Mr. Ljubicic, I'm now turning to you. I would like you to tell me if you have anything to say about your state of health or any other thing. You can share with us any comments you might have. I would like to take this opportunity to give you the possibility of speaking very openly and very frankly. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can stress here that I have no objection to the conditions of my stay in the Detention Unit or my treatment by the personnel there. As far as the proceedings against me are concerned, my only wish is that they come to an end as soon as possible. That's the only thing. The condition of my health is satisfactory, and everything else is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can assure you that I will personally make sure that this will be the case, and I have the opportunity and you have the opportunity as well, with the help of your counsel and with the cooperation of the Prosecution and with the kindness of Mr. Fourmy to work in that respect, I think things will be speeded up, and this is in keeping with the idea of justice that we all want to attain. Thank you very much. You can be seated. Any other comments? Any questions you might have?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have none, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Neither does the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I think that this Status Conference has come to an end and the hearing is adjourned. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: at 3.50 p.m.
